subject: Human Evolution
title: Cooperative Hunting
description: A quick, practical guide to Cooperative Hunting.

hook.text: A lone human can't take down a buffalo. Ten humans with a plan can corner one against a cliff.

buildup.text: Cooperative hunting requires shared goals, role assignment, and real-time communication.

discovery.text: Group hunting yields far more meat per person than solo efforts—enough to share with the whole band.

twist.text: Sharing the kill with non-hunters created reciprocal obligations and deepened social bonds.

climax.text: Hunting became a social glue: the meat mattered, but the cooperation mattered more.

punchline.text: The hunt fed bodies. Sharing the kill fed society.

quiz.question: Why was cooperative hunting socially important?
options: Sharing meat created bonds and reciprocal obligations
